newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds struggle to hold SYCOM levels.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds struggle to hold SYCOM levels.

text.p: *Australian bond futures struggled to hold the modest gains in SYCOM trade as a further slide in the Australian dollar knocked the short end lower.
*Westpac consumer sentiment survey due 2.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).
Australian bond futures struggled to hold the modest gains in SYCOM trade as a further slide in the Australian dollar knocked the short end lower.

The local dollar hit a fresh 18-month low of around US$0.7320/25, unnerving a debt market which has had its sights on a further easing in monetary policy, and possibly after next week's second quarter inflation and wages reports.
"It's all in the futures market at the moment, but bills are being dragged down as the dollar continues to head south," one bond trader said.
The September bill futures hit a 1-1/2 week low of 94.79.

At the low the contract has dropped 20 basis points since last Thursday's 94.99 peak which followed a weaker than expected employment report, but although easier, it still equates to a cash rate of over 25 basis points below official 5.5 percent interest rates.

Analysts pointed out that the local currency has still to test last year's US$0.7305 low and in trade weighted terms it is still holding above a five year average, leaving scope for the RBA to ease policy if it believes growth is too sluggish.
Bond futures had shown modest gains in after hours trade, underpinned by a stable U.S. Treasury market.

A slightly larger than expected 0.5 percent rise in U.S. retail sales failed to make much impression as it was accompanied by a downward revision to minus 0.3 percent from down 0.1 percent in the May sales report.
The U.S. market faces a barrage of data later on Wednesday with June CPI, along with May business inventories, industrial production and capacity utilisation all due for release.

Locally, data remains thin, although Westpac's latest consumer sentiment survey at 2.30 p.m. (0430 GMT) may generate more interest than usual, given that it has fallen three consecutive months to its lowest level since September 1995.

Local bonds continued Tuesday's mild underperformance against the U.S., but was little changed to Canada. New Zealand bond yields rose to firm up monetary conditions as the N.Z. dollar weakened. The yield curve flattened again, and was close to support at 75 basis points on the 3/10-year futures spread.
